name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Cranial Pressure Evacuation Drill
product_name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Cranial Pressure Evacuation Drill
description:
The Cranial Pressure Evacuation Drill is a precision field surgical instrument designed to perform emergency burr-hole trepanation — the controlled drilling of a small opening in the skull to relieve life-threatening intracranial pressure caused by hematoma, edema, or traumatic brain bleed. Arcturus developed the device for military combat medics who may encounter severe head trauma in environments where evacuation to a full surgical suite is impossible within the critical intervention window. The drill features a self-limiting depth governor that prevents penetration beyond the dura mater, a vacuum-sealed drainage port, and a real-time pressure differential sensor that tells the operator when sufficient decompression has been achieved.

The engineering is deliberately conservative: Arcturus resisted the temptation to automate the procedure fully, instead keeping a human hand on the instrument throughout. The device guides and limits but does not replace operator judgment, on the reasoning that a partially skilled medic with a governed tool makes better decisions in chaotic field conditions than a fully automated system that may misread ambiguous injury presentations. The housing is matte-black polymer over a titanium drill assembly, ruggedized for combat environments, and the entire kit including drainage tubing, sterile sleeve, and pressure sensor fits in a case the size of a large hardcover book.

It is called 'The Trepan' universally — medics, operators, and patients alike — though soldiers have also taken to calling it 'The Bishop's Key,' a reference both to its ecclesiastical shape and to the sense that its use represents a final negotiation between the living and the dead.

cultural_context: The Trepan occupies a specific psychological category in combat medicine culture: it is the tool that signals you are doing something that should not be done outside a hospital, and doing it anyway because the alternative is worse. Medics who have used it in the field report a lasting sense of having crossed a threshold. Among mercenary outfits, a medic known to carry and use the Trepan commands a particular kind of respect — and a particular kind of unease. In GLMZ's black-market surgical underground, modified civilian versions with the depth governor removed are used for more questionable cranial interventions, which has contributed to regulatory pressure on licensed distribution.

story_hooks: A modified Trepan with the depth governor removed has been used on a series of victims found in the outer wards — the penetration depth suggests someone was accessing rather than relieving, and the targets all survived with no memory of the procedure.

A corporate executive suffered a traumatic brain bleed during an ambush; the only person available with a Trepan is a player character with Field Surgical Certification Level 1 and a laminated diagram.

An Arcturus Defense Solutions shipment of Trepan kits has been intercepted — the drill sleeves have been swapped with non-sterile alternatives, and the first wave of field casualties from the new batch are developing post-procedural infections.

A street medic operating without a license has saved eleven lives with a black-market Trepan and is now facing prosecution; the families of the eleven are organizing in her defense, and Arcturus's legal team wants the device back as evidence.
